product_overview: A bilingual Agra taxi and tour platform consisting of a React customer website, an operations admin panel, and a Fastify API. The customer experience presents routes, vehicles, packages, fares, contact channels, and a five-step booking flow. The API is authoritative for fare calculations, bookings, payments, catalog, inquiries, reviews, and admin operations.
core_goals: Help customers discover Agra taxi, intercity, vehicle, and package services in English and Hindi.
Make transparent server-authoritative fares and booking information available before commitment.
Allow customers to contact the travel desk through call, WhatsApp, inquiries, and booking workflows.
Provide operations staff with role-aware dashboards for bookings, finance, catalog, reviews, inquiries, fares, and audit history.
Protect booking, payment, admin, webhook, and personally identifiable data from unauthorized access or mutation.
Keep the customer and admin clients maintainable as static deployments while the API remains the source of truth.

key_features.name: Customer marketing site
key_features.description: Responsive React pages for home, routes, services, fleet, packages, about, contact, FAQ, privacy, terms, and not-found handling.

key_features.name: Bilingual navigation
key_features.description: English and Hindi routes with language-aware content, metadata, canonical links, and hreflang parity.

key_features.name: Fare discovery
key_features.description: Route and vehicle selection with one-way/round-trip, passenger capacity, night allowance, package, and promo behavior.

key_features.name: Five-step booking
key_features.description: Search, vehicle selection, customer details, mock payment method, and confirmation ticket flow.

key_features.name: Location autocomplete
key_features.description: Location search backed by static curated places locally and LocationIQ when configured.

key_features.name: Admin operations
key_features.description: Dashboard and role-oriented screens for bookings, finance, catalog, reviews, inquiries, fares, and audit.

key_features.name: API security
key_features.description: CORS, helmet, rate limits, request IDs, schema validation, auth guards, role guards, raw webhook handling, and masked booking data.

key_features.name: Payments and webhooks
key_features.description: Checkout creation, idempotency, signed webhook reconciliation, refunds, and provider adapters.

user_flow_summary: Customer opens the site, switches English/Hindi, browses a route or package, and reaches a fare or contact CTA.
Customer completes the booking flow with a valid future date, route, vehicle, passenger count, contact details, and mock payment choice.
Customer receives a ticket identifier and can only retrieve a masked voucher after the required verification.
Customer sends an inquiry with valid name, phone, message, and optional email or trip interest.
Admin signs in with an isolated test role, navigates protected screens, and sees only permitted operations.
Admin reviews bookings, catalog, inquiries, reviews, fare information, finance, and audit records through API-backed flows.
API clients call health/readiness, fares, locations, bookings, payments, catalog, reviews, inquiries, and admin endpoints with valid and invalid inputs.
validation_criteria: All happy paths work at desktop and mobile viewport sizes without console errors or failed critical requests.
Deep links and browser refreshes resolve correctly for customer and admin routes.
English/Hindi content and fare values remain equivalent where the product contract requires parity.
Required fields, type boundaries, malformed values, unknown fields, XSS-like input, past dates, over-capacity vehicles, and invalid promo codes are rejected safely.
Unauthorized and wrong-role requests receive the expected 401/403 behavior and do not leak protected data.
Booking reads require full verification and return masked personal data.
Payment and refund operations are idempotent and never mark a booking paid from an unverified browser redirect.
API responses use the documented success/error envelope and include request IDs for failures.
Rate limiting, CORS, security headers, payload-size handling, webhook signatures, and secret redaction behave as designed.
Accessibility covers keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, semantic headings, contrast, reduced motion, and meaningful error announcements.
